steps.title: How Close Is Too Close?
steps.subtitle: Side event
steps.body: OEWG on PAROS, Fourth Session · November 23, 2026
steps.tagline: Building Shared Understanding of Satellite Behavior

steps.title: Proximity operations, close approaches, and shadowing
steps.subtitle: Official statements
steps.body: States describe these activities, in certain contexts, as concerning. Although each of these terms can be defined with physical conditions, states do not share their understanding of those conditions in public fora.

steps.title: Physical parameters as a basis for concern
steps.subtitle: A closer look
steps.body: Observed dynamics can help establish what is unusual. Whether they are disturbing also depends on context that States may not share. What physical basis of concern could we describe in common?

steps.title: How to describe an orbit
steps.subtitle: 01 · Orbital elements
steps.body: A satellite’s orbit can be described by six elements. Adjust them to see how its path changes around Earth.

steps.title: Orbital uncertainty
steps.subtitle: 02 · What a TLE does not say
steps.body: The ellipsoid is a hypothetical uncertainty region around the estimated satellite position. Public TLEs generally provide no covariance, so its size and shape are not measured uncertainty.

steps.title: Two neighboring GEO satellites
steps.subtitle: 03 · Shared orbital region
steps.body: Object A and Object B occupy nearby geostationary longitudes. Their TLE estimates can be updated as observations arrive.

steps.title: Relative motion
steps.subtitle: 04 · One satellite's frame
steps.body: Object B relocates while Object A anchors the rotating view. Separation distance, relative speed, and range rate answer different questions.

steps.title: Measurements through time
steps.subtitle: 05 · Geometry and charts
steps.body: Separation distance and relative speed change over time. Dwell is the cumulative time spent inside both selected thresholds.

steps.title: Conjunction versus close approach
steps.subtitle: 06 · Different questions
steps.body: Compare a brief, faster encounter with sustained slower proximity. Collision screening and descriptions of behavior have different purposes.

steps.title: Thresholds and dwell time
steps.subtitle: 07 · An explicit convention
steps.body: Set distance and speed thresholds. Gold intervals satisfy both; the cumulative duration is a descriptive measure, not a universal legal definition.

steps.title: Shadowing
steps.subtitle: 08 · Repeated proximity
steps.body: A synthetic sequence of orbital burns produces repeated approaches. The motion alone does not establish intent.

steps.title: Episodes of Concerning Satellite Proximity
steps.subtitle: Historical library
steps.body: Explore documented episodes, orbital reconstructions, and linked source records.

steps.title: Limits of public reconstructions
steps.subtitle: What the model cannot establish
steps.body: Sparse observations, dated TLEs, unknown covariance, and unobserved maneuvers limit what a public reconstruction can claim.

steps.title: Uncertainty in three scenarios
steps.subtitle: Illustrative covariance
steps.body: The ellipsoids are illustrative, not measured covariance from a TLE.

steps.title: Future research
steps.subtitle: From episodes to baselines
steps.body: Congestion, statistical baselines, and proximity between energy-related space systems.

steps.title: Further behavioral questions
steps.subtitle: Future research
steps.body: Energy-space proximity and sustained line of sight are distinct from separation distance alone.

steps.title: Questions for discussion
steps.subtitle: OEWG on PAROS
steps.body:
Which measurable characteristics of satellite behavior are most useful for distinguishing routine proximity operations from activities that may warrant concern, clarification, or consultation?

Where might states’ interpretations of close approaches, shadowing, and other proximity operations converge or diverge, and what additional operational context is necessary to understand those differences?

What information could states reasonably share to substantiate their concerns or enable independent assessments, without disclosing sensitive space domain awareness capabilities?

How might shared physical descriptions and evidentiary practices contribute to voluntary transparency and confidence-building measures, legally binding instruments, or both?
